rule_citation: N.C.G.S. 62-126.4 (H589, S.L. 2017-192); NCUC Docket E-100 Sub 180 Order Approving Revised Net Metering Tariffs (Mar 23 2023) + Order Granting Extension (May 17 2023) and Duke compliance tariffs filed Apr 3 2023 (DEC Leaf 72 Rider NM, Leaf 143 Rider NMB, Leaf 141 Rider RSC; DEP Riders NM-5, NMB-1, RSC-2); NC Interconnection Procedures (NCIP) eff. June 14 2019, Docket E-100 Sub 101 (text: https://www.duke-energy.com/_/media/pdfs/rates/ncinterconnections-dep.pdf?la=en)
applies_to: IOU only (Duke Energy Carolinas, Duke Energy Progress, Dominion Energy NC). EMCs and municipals are not rate-regulated by NCUC and are not required to offer net metering; they set their own rules (see utility file)
nem_successor: Legacy Rider NM closed to new residential applicants (tariff text July 1 2023; extended to 9/30/2023 by May 17 2023 order); legacy residential participants must transfer to Rider NMB or another rider by Jan 1 2027. Successors: Rider RSC (Residential Solar Choice; requires Schedule R-TOU-CPP; netting within each TOU period incl. separate CPP period; NEEC for net excess; NBC; grid access fee above 15 kW; minimum bill) and Rider NMB (Net Metering Bridge; same credit/NBC/minimum bill but on any rate; annual kW enrollment caps; closed to new participants Jan 1 2027; Bridge Rate Period up to 15 calendar years from submission date of the applicable interconnection application, then transfer to RSC). Non-residential Rider NM not closed by these tariffs. BATTERY RETROFIT: riders require written notice of any Nameplate Capacity change within 60 days; neither NMB nor RSC text says a battery addition restarts the 15-yr Bridge term or forces a move to RSC - Unclear (a new interconnection application for the battery could arguably be 'the applicable interconnection application'; not addressed). MID-TRANSITION: legacy-to-NMB migration Jan 2027
nem_cap_res_kw: 20 kW AC and not more than estimated maximum monthly demand of the residence (Riders NMB/RSC)
nem_cap_nonres_kw: 1000 kW (legacy Rider NM, lesser of estimated max annual kW demand or 1,000 kW)
nem_aggregate_cap: No statewide aggregate cap. Rider NMB annual enrollment capacity (kW AC, first-come first-served, reserved at interconnection application): DEC 2023 14,500 / 2024 31,900 / 2025 35,100 / 2026 38,700; DEP 2023 16,350 / 2024 35,900 / 2025 39,500 / 2026 43,500. Applicants after the annual cap must reapply next year or take RSC. Current subscription level not verified
nem_sizing_rule: Residential (NMB/RSC): nameplate <= lesser of estimated max monthly demand of residence or 20 kW AC. Non-residential legacy NM: <= lesser of estimated max annual kW demand or 1,000 kW
export_credit_value: Net Excess Energy Credit (NEEC): DEC 3.35 c/kWh, DEP 3.40 c/kWh (compliance tariffs eff. July 2023; later biennial updates not checked). Legacy Rider NM: 1:1 retail kWh (TOU customers netted by period)
credit_rollover: Successor riders: monthly net excess credited in dollars at NEEC; credits roll forward (no forfeiture per installer summary). Legacy Rider NM: kWh credits roll monthly, forfeited annually
annual_true_up: Legacy Rider NM only: unused credits forfeited June 1 (DEC) / May 31 (DEP) with no payment. Successor riders: no annual forfeiture (monthly NEEC crediting)
ic_standard: NCIP (June 14 2019) Attachment 4: IEEE 1547 + IEEE 1547.1 testing, UL 1741 certified equipment (edition not specified). IEEE 1547-2018 / UL 1741-SB implementation tracked by annual utility reports in Docket E-100 Sub 101B (Duke report Apr 1 2020; DENC Mar 15 2021); a dated mandatory 1547-2018 cutover was not found
ic_fast_track_kw: Certified UL inverter-based only. Line <5 kV: 100 kW (500 kW if on mainline and <=2.5 circuit miles from substation); 5-15 kV: 1 MW (2 MW); 15-35 kV: 2 MW; >=35 kV ineligible
ic_simplified_kw: 20 kW (Section 2 20 kW Inverter Process for certified inverter-based facilities)
ic_application_fee: $200 non-refundable (20 kW Inverter Process form, 2019 NCIP; 2015 NCIP was $100); Fast Track $750 (>20-100 kW), $1,000 (>100 kW-2 MW); Supplemental Review deposit $750 (>20-100 kW) and higher above; $500 pre-application report; $500 change of ownership; Study Process deposit + $1/kW AC capped at $100,000 aggregate
ic_study_trigger_kw: Above Fast Track limits (100 kW-2 MW depending on line voltage/location), non-inverter or uncertified equipment, lines >=35 kV, or failure of Fast Track/Supplemental Review screens -> Section 4 Study Process (System Impact + Facilities studies)
external_disconnect: Utility discretion (NCIP 6.16: utility may require lockable, visible, accessible manual load-break disconnect; for certified inverter-based <=10 kW where not otherwise code-required, utility reimburses reasonable cost)
insurance_required: Residential <=250 kW: homeowner's policy with >= $100,000/occurrence liability; non-residential <=250 kW: CGL >= $300,000; non-residential >250 kW: CGL >= $1,000,000 (NCIP 6.15; self-insurance allowed if creditworthy)
ic_timeline_days: 20 kW process: utility has 15 business days to verify screens; Fast Track initial review within 15 business days of complete request; witness test within 10 business days of Certificate of Completion
storage_allowed: Yes-with-conditions (NCIP defines Generating Facility to include storage and asks kWh; adding storage/DC equipment not a Material Modification if output profile unchanged, NCIP 1.5.2. NEM riders admit only storage charged solely from onsite renewables)
grid_charging_allowed: No - Riders NM, NMB and RSC (DEC and DEP) only admit 'an energy storage device configured to receive electrical charge solely from onsite renewable energy generation'. A grid-charged battery would have to sit outside net metering (non-NEM arrangement not verified)
non_export_option: Partial: NCIP Interconnection Request asks for an hourly max import/export profile (flows above it = Adverse Operating Effect), and a Standby Generating Facility with zero export gets expedited Section 4 study (NCIP 1.8.3.4). No dedicated non-export Fast Track screen found
storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear - 20 kW AC cap applies to 'Nameplate Capacity of Customer's installed generation system and equipment'; NBC/GAF billed per kW DC for solar or kW AC for non-solar; battery kW treatment not stated
standby_charge: Not a standby charge per se: NBC $0.28/kW-mo (DEC) / $0.62/kW-mo (DEP) on nameplate; RSC Grid Access Fee $2.05 (DEC) / $1.50 (DEP) per kW above 15 kW; monthly minimum bill (customer+distribution portion) $22 (DEC NMB, DEC RSC, DEP NMB) / $28 (DEP RSC). DEP Rider NM-5: standby not required for residential or general service <=100 kW
standby_threshold_kw: 15 kW (RSC grid access fee); 100 kW general service (DEP legacy NM standby waiver)

jurisdiction_body: Public Service Commission of South Carolina (PSCSC); Office of Regulatory Staff
rule_citation: S.C. Code 58-40-20 as amended by Act 62 of 2019 (SC Energy Freedom Act) - Solar Choice Metering; PSCSC Order 2021-390 (Duke, Docket 2020-264-E) and Order 2021-391 (DESC, Docket 2020-229-E); Order 2025-453 (DEC Rider NMT); SC Generator Interconnection Procedures eff. June 18 2021, Docket 2019-326-E, Order 2021-439 (https://etariff.psc.sc.gov/Uploads/tariffFile/0d678dc4-2ccb-4938-8f9c-cf3982a3b781); DESC Solar Choice rider https://etariff.psc.sc.gov/Uploads/tariffFile/36cec7b8-fe00-411a-87a1-320edcf87331; DEC Rider NMT https://etariff.psc.sc.gov/Uploads/tariffFile/ec070b41-9f5f-4c6f-a11a-480e0b73b559
applies_to: IOU only (Duke Energy Carolinas, Duke Energy Progress, Dominion Energy South Carolina). Santee Cooper (state authority), electric cooperatives and munis are not bound by these tariffs and set their own net metering/interconnection rules (see utility file)
nem_successor: Act 62 Solar Choice Metering tariffs for applications on/after June 1 2021: Duke Rider RSC (requires Schedule R-STOU; netting within each TOU period, CPP exports netted against On-Peak; net excess per TOU period credited at avoided-cost-based rate; NBC per kW; minimum bill); DESC Solar Choice rider to Rate 5 (TOU kWh netting by period, kWh bank to November; minimum term 10 yrs). Legacy Duke Rider RNM (1:1): applications before 5/16/2019 through 12/31/2025; 5/16/2019-5/31/2021 through 5/31/2029. MID-TRANSITION: DEC Rider NMT (Order 2025-453, eff. 1/1/2026) takes legacy RNM/IRSC customers for up to 10 yrs (to 12/31/2035 for pre-5/16/2019 apps; 6/1/2029-5/31/2039 for later apps) with monthly netting and NEEC for excess, then Rider RSC. BATTERY RETROFIT: NMT/RSC dates are keyed to the 'original interconnection application date for the generation system' and customers must report Nameplate Capacity changes within 60 days; neither rider says a battery addition resets dates - Unclear, but the storage-charging restriction below would apply
nem_cap_res_kw: 20 kW AC (Act 62 customer-generator definition; Duke RSC/NMT and DESC Solar Choice riders)
nem_aggregate_cap: None stated in the Solar Choice riders read (legacy DESC 2015 rider had a 0.2% of SC retail peak cap; that rider is closed)
nem_sizing_rule: Customer-generator must be 'intended primarily to offset part or all of the customer-generator's own electrical energy requirements'; <=20 kW AC residential
export_credit_value: DEC Rider RSC: $0.0397/kWh net excess per TOU period (Leaf 136 eff. 1/1/2024); DEC Rider NMT: 4.19 c/kWh (eff. 1/1/2026). DESC Solar Choice: excess kWh offsets same-TOU-period usage in later months; unused bank paid at avoided cost (Rate PR-1 off-peak winter energy credit) each November
credit_rollover: Duke: monthly dollar credit at NEEC (no kWh bank). DESC: kWh bank rolls monthly within TOU period, cash-out at avoided cost in November
annual_true_up: DESC: November billing cycle, unused excess kWh paid at avoided cost and bank zeroed. Duke RSC/NMT: none (monthly crediting)
ic_standard: SC Generator Interconnection Procedures (June 18 2021) Attachment: IEEE 1547 + IEEE 1547.1 testing, UL certified inverters (edition not specified in text). No dated IEEE 1547-2018/UL 1741-SB mandate found
ic_fast_track_kw: Certified UL inverter-based only. Line <5 kV: 100 kW (500 kW on mainline <=2.5 circuit miles from substation); 5-25 kV: 1 MW (2 MW); >=25 kV not eligible
ic_simplified_kw: 20 kW (Section 2 20 kW Inverter Process; utility reserves circuit capacity per phase for <=20 kW projects)
ic_application_fee: Fast Track/20 kW: $100 (<=20 kW), $250 (>20-100 kW), $500 (>100 kW-2 MW); $50 transfer of ownership; Study Process deposits separate (Duke cluster appendix $10,000 study deposit)
ic_study_trigger_kw: Above Fast Track limits (100 kW-2 MW by voltage/location) or failure of Fast Track screens -> Section 4 serial Study Process, or Commission-authorized Cluster Study (utility appendix)
external_disconnect: Required for 20 kW Inverter Process per its Terms and Conditions (manual load-break disconnect immediately adjacent to utility meter unless utility agrees otherwise); utility discretion above; utility reimburses cost for certified inverter-based <=10 kW when not code-required
insurance_required: Residential <=250 kW: homeowner's policy >= $100,000/occurrence; non-residential <=250 kW: CGL >= $300,000; non-residential >250 kW higher (amount not read)
ic_timeline_days: 20 kW process: utility has 15 business days to complete screening; witness test within 10 business days or deemed waived
storage_allowed: Yes-with-conditions (customer-generator definition includes energy storage charged solely from onsite renewables; SC GIP application collects storage data)
grid_charging_allowed: No - Act 62 customer-generator definition, repeated in Duke RSC/NMT and DESC Solar Choice riders, covers only 'an energy storage device configured to receive electrical charge solely from an onsite renewable energy resource'
non_export_option: Unclear - no defined non-export/limited-export screen found in SC GIP text searched
storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear - 20 kW AC cap applies to 'Nameplate Capacity of Customer's installed generation system and equipment'; NBC billed on kW DC for solar or kW AC for non-solar
standby_charge: No standby charge for Solar Choice residential. Duke: non-bypassable charge per nameplate kW (NMT: $0.45/kW for apps on/after 6/1/2021; RSC amount not read); NMT minimum customer & distribution charge $10; RSC minimum bill = Basic Facilities Charge plus rate-schedule minimum. DESC Solar Choice minimum bill $13.50/month

jurisdiction_body: Georgia Public Service Commission (Georgia Power); EMC and municipal governing bodies for their own systems
rule_citation: Georgia Cogeneration and Distributed Generation Act of 2001, O.C.G.A. 46-3-50 to 46-3-56; Georgia Power Schedule RNR-11 (eff. Jan 2023 bills; GPSC Dockets 4822 and 16573); Georgia Power Rules and Regulations Section G (Customer Generation) https://www.georgiapower.com/content/dam/georgia-power/pdfs/business-pdfs/tariffs/2023/Rules-Regs.pdf; GPC BTM Interconnection Summary (Residential) rev. 08.15.2025 https://www.georgiapower.com/content/dam/georgia-power/pdfs/company-pdfs/solar-pdfs/btm-distribution-interconnection-summary-residential.pdf
applies_to: All utilities for the statutory purchase obligation ('electric service provider' includes electric utilities, EMCs and municipal utilities); PSC sets rates/interconnection terms only for Georgia Power; EMCs and munis set price and interconnection rules through their own governing bodies (46-3-56(b),(d))
nem_successor: Georgia Power RNR-Monthly Netting (5,000-customer pilot) closed to new participants; non-transferable, 15-year term expiring no later than 12/31/2038, then automatic move to RNR-Instantaneous Netting. New customers: RNR-Instantaneous Netting (every kWh exported at any instant credited at Solar Avoided Energy Cost + 4 c/kWh adder)
nem_cap_res_kw: 10 kW AC (statute and RNR; capacity = aggregate inverter nameplate at service point)
nem_cap_nonres_kw: 100 kW (statute); Georgia Power RNR allows commercial up to 250 kW AC (100-250 kW limited to 125% of prior-year metered peak demand)
nem_aggregate_cap: 0.2% of the utility's previous-year annual peak demand (O.C.G.A. 46-3-56(a); GPC RNR-Instantaneous first-come first-served to 0.2%); once subscribed, provider may purchase at a price set by PSC/governing body. Subscription level not verified
nem_sizing_rule: GPC: 100-250 kW commercial <=125% of preceding year's metered peak demand; no residential consumption-based rule in RNR-11
export_credit_value: GPC RNR-Instantaneous: Solar Avoided Energy Cost (updated annually under Renewable Cost Benefit framework, Docket 16573; value not read) + 4 c/kWh Renewable Generation Adder. RNR-Monthly (legacy): excess kWh offsets monthly consumption, remainder at Solar Avoided Energy Cost
credit_rollover: Monthly: credits summed monthly and applied to that month's bill (carryover of credits exceeding the bill not stated in tariff)
ic_standard: Georgia Power: Southern Company DER Parallel Operation policy; inverters and AC-coupled battery gateways must be listed UL 1741 SB and IEEE 1547-2018 (BTM Summary 2025); >=250 kW needs local communications interface per IEEE 1547-2018 (Rules and Regs G.3). Statute requires NEC/NESC/IEEE/UL compliance only
ic_fast_track_kw: No statewide tiered fast-track; Georgia Power uses a single PowerClerk BTM process below 250 kW
ic_application_fee: Georgia Power: one-time $100 residential, $200 commercial/industrial; for <250 kW covers review, metering/programming and witness testing (Rules and Regs G.4)
ic_study_trigger_kw: 250 kW (Georgia Power: system impact study + witness testing mandatory at >=250 kW; smaller units only if deemed a risk)
external_disconnect: Required by Georgia Power (one-line must show generation AC disconnect(s) isolating the facility, visible load-break details per Construction Guidelines); no statewide rule
insurance_required: Statute bars providers from requiring additional liability insurance from a compliant customer generator (O.C.G.A. 46-3-56(e))
storage_allowed: Yes-with-conditions (GPC: UL 1741 SB/IEEE 1547-2018 inverters; backup-capable systems need open-transition, mechanically interlocked transfer switch and DB 18-23 non-export form)
grid_charging_allowed: Unclear - RNR-11 credits any metered 'Excess Energy' delivered to the grid and says nothing about battery charging source; GPC summary describes batteries for 'self-consumption only' use; no rule found that bars or permits crediting of grid-charged exports
non_export_option: Yes - Georgia Power Energy Offset Only (EOO) agreement (no export, no compensation, utility may require export-prevention equipment; default if customer does not pick a program); DB 18-23 non-exporting generator form
storage_counts_toward_cap: Yes (Georgia Power): AC capacity is aggregate inverter nameplate at the service point; a battery system with maximum inverter capability >10 kW (even if derated) makes a residential customer ineligible for RNR
standby_charge: None found. RNR single-directional metering charge $5.97/mo (single-phase) or $12.66/mo (poly-phase) where used; bi-directional metering free
